title: In-Context Black-Box Optimization with Unreliable Feedback
claim: Existing amortized optimizers lack test-time auxiliary feedback and feedback-aware pretraining; ours pretrains on varied-reliability feedback and uses it at deployment.
layout: Top row of 3 colored pipeline panels, comparison checkmark table below
description: The top half has three rounded panels, pink, green and blue, read left to right. Arrows labeled Training and Inference link them. The pink Feedback Prior panel has a legend (f_truth, a ±2σ band, f_feedback) and three small curve plots labeled globally useful, locally useful and misleading. The green Model panel stacks Features and Feedback inside an Embedder, then a Transformer, then Posterior and Policy heads, with arrows pointing upward. The blue Deployment panel shows a Data box with Features (lab icons) and Feedback (person and scatter icons), feeding a History cylinder. Curved arrows connect History to Sample in a loop. The bottom half is a comparison table. Rows are Vanilla BO, πBO/CoExBO, PFNs4BO, BoFormer, NAP/PABBO/TAMO, then a highlighted FICBO row. Columns are four capabilities, marked with red crosses and green checks. FICBO is the only row with checks in every column.
caption: Feedback-informed in-context black-box optimization (FICBO) and related work. During training, tasks are sampled from a feedback prior with auxiliary sources of varying reliability. A transformer learns both posterior prediction and query selection from features and feedback. At deployment, it conditions on the optimization history and the available feedback to guide search.
abstract: Black-box optimization in science and engineering often comes with side information: experts, simulators, pretrained predictors, or heuristics can suggest promising candidates. Such feedback can accelerate search, but can also be biased, input-dependent, or misleading. Feedback-aware Bayesian optimization methods typically handle tasks independently, limiting adaptation across feedback sources. In-context optimizers enable cross-task adaptation, but usually rely only on optimization history at test time. We study feedback-informed in-context black-box optimization (FICBO), where a pretrained optimizer conditions on both the observed history and cheap auxiliary feedback for the current candidate set. We introduce structured priors over how auxiliary feedback relates to the objective, and use them to pretrain a feedback-aware transformer across regimes ranging from highly informative to misleading. At test time, the model estimates source reliability in context by comparing observed objective values with auxiliary signals, improving query selection. On synthetic and real-world tasks, FICBO effectively exploits informative feedback while remaining robust to weak or misleading sources. Empirical investigations further illustrate how the model perceives test-time sources, offering insights into its interpretability and decision-making process.
